title: European Council agrees to open EU accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova
body:
The European Council met on Thursday, 14 December 2023, with discussions continuing on 15 December. According to an account published by the Czech government on 16 December, EU leaders agreed to start accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova. Georgia received candidate-country status, and leaders agreed that negotiations with Bosnia and Herzegovina would open once the country met the required membership criteria. A summit with Western Balkan leaders was held beforehand, and the EU adopted a declaration with the Western Balkan countries supporting their European perspective and gradual integration into EU areas.

Leaders did not agree on revising the 2021-2027 Multiannual Financial Framework, which included a 50 billion euro instrument for Ukraine. Hungary opposed the plan. Czech Prime Minister Petr Fiala said 26 member states, including the Czech Republic, could have backed a compromise but Hungary did not. The debate was to continue at an extraordinary meeting, possibly as early as late January 2024.

The Council also condemned Russia's war against Ukraine, committed to tighter sanctions and welcomed the adoption of the 12th sanctions package. It agreed to deepen cooperation on buying defence equipment. The same meeting addressed the Hamas attacks on Israel and the use of migrants as a tool of hybrid warfare, citing pressure on the Polish border and incidents on the Russian-Finnish border.
